title: Show the source commit in `athena --version`
summary: `athena --version` currently prints only the Cargo package version, because clap's `version` attribute ignores the commit that `build_info()` already embeds (set by xtask). I read the request as making the version string include the source commit and a dirty/unknown marker.

defaults_applied.how: Rust only; no build.rs or scripts added, reusing the existing build_info() and xtask env plumbing.
Add a test for the new version formatting.
Reuse existing build_info() rather than a new git-describe crate or build script.
One focused change to the version string only.

assumptions: ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT is already set by `xtask` (xtask/src/main.rs:250) when installing, so only the --version output needs to change; no build.rs is added.
'Which build setup adopted' means the installed binary's commit, so a commit hash plus dirty flag is enough.
The binary is the `athena` bin in crates/athena-cli, whose clap `version` currently prints only CARGO_PKG_VERSION.

acceptance_criteria.text: `athena --version` output is built from wiring::build_info() and includes the package version and the source commit (short or full hash); clap's default CARGO_PKG_VERSION-only version string is replaced.
A build with no embedded commit, or with ATHENA_BUILD_DIRTY not 'false', is shown as such (e.g. 'unknown' and/or 'dirty'), consistent with build_info()'s dirty rule.
A unit or integration test covers the version-string formatting for clean, dirty, and unknown-commit builds.
Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- --version` (no build env set): it exits 0 and prints the version with an 'unknown' commit marked as dirty/unknown.

out_of_scope: Changing how xtask computes the commit or dirty flag
Adding a build.rs or git-describe dependency
Changing recorded Build fields in job records
departures: Small, well-localized change with existing build_info() plumbing, so slightly higher pass probability and lower cost than the reference.
